title: Can crypto CNNs trade less?
intro: We explored daily prices for eight cryptocurrencies. Daily CNN rebalancing incurred substantial assumed costs; trading less helped in some windows, but a stable advantage remains unproven.
notice: This is retrospective research, not a fresh holdout, live performance or competition returns. The fixed 2023–2025 universe has selection bias; fills and asset events remain unverified. The data and results have not passed formal research acceptance.

tableIntro: These medians assume a 0.35% one-way total cost per trade, not a verified exchange fee. Each window starts in cash and closes its positions. They are not the return of one continuous three-year account.

limits: The volatility overlay matches target exposure; realized risk can still differ across portfolios.
The image model predicts absolute returns; the numeric model ranks coins. Differences cannot be attributed to image input alone.
Signals use the daily close and simulated fills use the next daily open. Crypto trades continuously, so the adjacent open can be optimistic; an extra day's delay also changes the holding period.
The fixed eight-asset universe is not a point-in-time market history. Token events, source data and actual execution conditions remain to be checked.
Historical sentiment access, coverage and cost are unverified; no sentiment model was run.
These are feasibility settings. Each image model trains on just 200 images for two epochs. Results need new data for further testing.
methodBody: We used 2023–2025 UTC daily spot data for eight USDT pairs from Binance monthly archives. Source and historical availability have not been independently accepted. The numeric CNN uses a 400-day span, including 120 days of validation, to predict five-day outcomes in later windows. The image CNN trains separately in each window on 200 images for two epochs. Most of the eight test windows cover 85 days; the last covers 37, with gaps between windows. Each window starts in cash and liquidates at the end.
riskNote: Research is separate from order execution. These simulations do not establish actual exchange fills, market impact or future performance.
